angle: VERTICAL SLICES: one whole user journey per run of batches, each batch ending deployable. Order: the editor (B1 frame, B2 content, B3 design drawer and gallery, B4 personal info and cover letter, B5 ATS, improve, download, share), then Documents with the shared shell (B6) and New/Import/Legal/Public (B7), then Applications (B8 board/list/insights, B9 job drawer and form), then Projects (B10 core, B11 board/issue/backlog), then phone (B12 phone editor and design, B13 phone shell/Documents/Applications, B14 phone Projects plus the three read-only project views and the closing sweep). 14 batches, 1,223 parity rows (every row of the 7 area files, including the rows added by review and the drawn-but-not-live rows) each owned by exactly one batch (verified by a script over the final files; counts per batch: B1 88, B2 78, B3 98, B4 90, B5 98, B6 91, B7 76, B8 90, B9 72, B10 92, B11 92, B12 102, B13 95, B14 61).
principles: Vertical slice rule: a batch finishes one journey step end to end (code, tests, bug hunt, CI proof) and its head is deployable (full gate green). Shared pieces are built only when the first slice needs them: tokens and test helpers in B1, a hooks-first commit (stable data-testid, helper migration, no visual change) at the start of B2 and B6, the two top bars in B6, kit variants where first used. No up-front 'design system' batch.

The parity rule is the spec and the canvas is a layout: for every CHANGED / MISSING row the build follows the Fix column of parity/<area>.md (restore the live control inside the nearest drawn home, one menu or drawer away). A row 'drawn but not in the live app' is built only if it is the same function under another name; otherwise it is PARKED and the live behaviour wins. Nothing new is invented.

Interim phone guard: the editor, the workspace shell and the Dashboard already have phone branches. Every desktop batch keeps them working (nothing becomes unreachable at 375 px; Cypress 26-mobile-layout and a 375 px Playwright reachability check run in each batch gate) but does not redraw them. The phone look is B12 to B14, which reuse the finished panels with max-md variants.

Hooks first, then restyle. For a pure move or restyle the fail-first test pins the NEW place (parity/_tests.md section 9): (a) reachability: open through the new opener, find the control inside the new region by data-testid; (b) negative twin: the old path is gone (the old tab button is not in the DOM) while the old URL still lands in the right place; (c) same write: the moved control calls the same store action with the same key and value (reuse the walker registry ids); (d) control count: the union of controls across regrouped views equals a hard-coded count taken from tests/pdf/parity/walk-cache.mjs; (e) render counts (165, 173) for anything inside the editor's keystroke path.

Single-owner files are serialised by batch order (one batch runs at a time) and by cluster inside a batch. Owners: Editor.jsx, EditorHeader.jsx, useEditorTab.js, EditorPreviewPane.jsx, EditorTabContent.jsx, LayoutToggle.jsx = B1 (B12 edits only the isMobile branch); DesignPanel*.jsx and TemplateGallery.jsx = B3 (B12 phone variants only); PersonalInfoEditor*.jsx, HeaderSpacingControls.jsx, CoverLetterPanel*.jsx = B4; SectionEditor*.jsx, RichTextEditor.jsx, EditorResumeTab.jsx = B2; AtsCheckerPanel.jsx, BulletOptimizerModal.jsx, ExportDropdown.jsx, ShareLinkModal.jsx = B5; Dashboard.jsx, AuthBar.jsx, ResumeCard.jsx, shell/TopBar.jsx, shell/WorkspaceLayout.jsx = B6 (later batches B8, B10, B13 make small named edits, never in parallel); AppRoutes.jsx = B7 only; src/index.css = B1 tokens, then B6 shared classes, then each later batch appends inside its own marked block through ONE cluster; tests/pdf/parity registries = B3 (labels), B4 and B5 (letter, ATS, export, share rows).

Start-up path has about 0 kB spare: all editor, Applications, Projects and workspace-shell code is lazy (zero cost). Only B6, B7 and B13 touch start-up files; B6 starts with offsets (lazy NewLetterModal and its Dialog closure, lazy CareerHistoryPanel on the Dashboard, dynamic JSON Resume import if needed) and must END with at least 3 kB spare as a reserve for B7 and B13. Any batch that edits a start-up file runs tests/pdf/71-startup-chunks.test.mjs in its targeted dispatch and reports the margin.

Render-count discipline: tests/pdf/165-perf4-editor-render-count and 173-editor-header-render-count are green at the end of every editor batch and every later batch that touches components under Editor (B12). Memoised editor parts take stable props (useStableActions, useStableObject, useSameList), no router hook, no router Link; the save chip is a self-contained leaf.

Keep the label contract. The visible strings tests share (Design & Customize, Back to dashboard, Section options, Rename resume, Split view, Editor only, Preview only, Drag to resize panel, Hide on resume, Delete entry, Delete application, Click to add to Skills, Download .txt, aria-label Section title) change only in the batch that owns them, in one commit with the tests, with evidence. Walker rule: never rename a control so that two controls collapse in the walker signature, and keep 'Reset' in a reset control's name.

Tests run only on CI. Per batch: failfirst dispatch (one machine per fix commit) then ONE targeted dispatch (new tests + every test that mounts a touched component + 71-startup-chunks when start-up files changed + named Playwright/Cypress specs), then ONE full gate (ci.yml, no inputs) on the final head. The lead reads each log itself. Stale tests are rewritten to the intended behaviour with evidence in the commit message, never weakened, skipped or deleted.

Pushes go to claude/wonderful-maxwell-vu8xqw only, never master. Commits are authored and committed as sairamgudiputi <sairamgudiputi8@gmail.com> with no trailers and no mention of Claude or AI. Accessibility items (aria, contrast, focus, target sizes) are noted in the batch report, never planned or built.

Pure restyle needs no new function test beyond the existing tests staying green plus one structural test where the layout changed; every behaviour fix found by a bug hunt gets its own failfirst-proven test.

Each batch brief carries a 'layout deltas' table written by the lead from the Fix column of its CHANGED / MISSING rows (how the drawn layout bends to hold the live function). That table is the correction to the canvas, so no board is redrawn before the build.

canvasCorrections.whenAndHow: No blocking canvas correction pass. Of 1,223 rows, about 40 percent are MISSING and 11 percent CHANGED, but the audit shows that nearly all MISSING rows mean 'the board draws a container (a card, a menu, a drawer, a collapsed disclosure) without its contents', not 'the design drops the function': the Fix column already names the nearest drawn home, and the parity rule says the layout bends, the function does not. A redraw of the 39 boards needs the rig, two agents and at least one 2-hour window per area, delays Batch 1, and the owner has not yet approved the canvas (edits to it are out of scope for this task). Instead: (1) each batch brief starts with a 'layout deltas' table (CHANGED rows only, about 5 to 25 lines per batch) that says how the drawn layout bends, written from the parity Fix column at step 1 of the batch protocol; (2) the render check (step 3) compares the build with the board AND the delta table; (3) where a delta needs a real design call that the Fix column does not settle (the Documents card menu, the Jobs list column set, the section overflow menu, Design drawer panes, the phone sheets), the lead picks the conservative option (live control kept, one menu or drawer away) and records it in the batch report; (4) OPTIONAL and non-blocking, after B14 only: refresh the canvas boards from the built UI so the owner has an accurate record (a single small workflow, no gate). A blocking redraw would be justified only if the owner overrules the parity rule's 'layout bends' reading for a specific board.

sharedRisks: Start-up path has about 0 kB spare (71-startup-chunks): B6 must create and hand over a 3 kB reserve before B7 and B13; a shared module imported by both the Dashboard and a lazy page is hoisted into the entry chunk, so every new helper must be checked against tests/pdf/startup-modules.mjs. If the reserve cannot be reached the only options (lazy Dashboard or raising the 1,100 kB cap in two files) are the owner's call.

Test blast radius: about 400 of 1,065 node files, 15 of 33 Cypress and 4 of 11 Playwright specs touch UI. The hooks-first commits (B2, B6) and the helpers of B1 keep the churn inside a few files; 173 (872 lines) is a rewrite; about 56 class-pin files of the 103-r4-dph / dvis families must be restated on new markup, never weakened.

Render counts: 165 and 173 pin that a keystroke renders only the typed field's own part; any unstable prop, router hook in a memoised part, or new context in the editor tree fails them. They are the failfirst proof for the editor chrome.

Walker (tests/pdf/parity) and parity-ui-controls.spec are the browser and node twins that walk every control: a renamed control that collides in the signature, a lost 'Reset' in a reset name, or a panel mounted only behind new props fails them; the groups, view and rail props must default to today's behaviour.

Single-owner files across 14 sequential batches (Editor.jsx, EditorHeader.jsx, TopBar.jsx, Dashboard.jsx, AuthBar.jsx, index.css, AppRoutes.jsx) need exactly one cluster per batch; later batches edit them only for the named small changes (B8 Dashboard link, B10 TopBar projects menu, B12 phone branch, B13 phone classes).

Many MISSING rows have no drawn home (undrawn menus, popovers, disclosures, entry forms, panes): the per-batch layout-delta table is the safeguard, and each decision must keep the live control one menu or drawer away.

Known intermittent test J-30 (tests/pdf/81-job-tracker-session.test.mjs) on shard 2/6 and the shard-2 flake 102-r4-dout-09-letter-title-weight: rerun failed jobs once for a known flake, record both attempts, never skip; J-30 is root-caused in B8.

Window cadence: B1, B6, B10, B11 and B12 are the heaviest and may spill into a second window; because only one batch runs at a time the plan estimates about 16 windows for 14 batches. Each cluster is merged as soon as it lands so a window end never leaves a half-merged batch.

Phone is last: until B12 to B14 the phone layouts are old but functional through the interim guard; a desktop batch that breaks a phone function is a regression of that batch, caught by Cypress 26-mobile-layout and the 375 px Playwright check in every gate.
